title: How qteasy's parts fit together
summary: Local data, a data panel, strategies run by an Operator, then backtest, optimization, and simulated live trading.
narrative:
qteasy is one pipeline. This card only names the parts. The numbers below name the next windows. A later question may refer to a number; explain that item from its card.

1. Local data. Downloads land in a local store, then become information you can read. History-shaped series can sit in a HistoryPanel.
2. Strategies and Operator. Built-in or custom strategies declare the data they need. An Operator runs them.
3. Backtest. It evaluates a strategy on historical data and reports the result.
4. Optimization. It searches parameters of a strategy.
5. Simulated live. The same strategy logic runs on a live-style schedule. Ask can explain the boundary. It does not start a trader or send orders.

Naming a module does not download data, run a backtest, or start simulated live trading.
